Nov 9 : Meta Platforms said on Monday it would expand its AI age-estimation technology globally to move millions more teens on Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if they have given birth dates showing they are adults, as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users. Here are more details: • Teen Accounts, available on Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, include built-in protections that automatically limit who can contact teens, the content they see and their time on the apps • Parents in the US will begin receiving Instagram notifications this month explaining how teens are placed in age-appropriate protections, Meta said

BERLIN, Nov 9 : Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has questioned whether playmaker Jamal Musiala can ever reach top form again after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Musiala, who is close to a comeback from an injury, collapsed twice in a few days in August, including six minutes after coming off the bench in Bayern's 4-2 friendly win at Heidenheim. He was later diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Musiala broke his leg at the Club World Cup in 2025, missing half of last season before a comeback in early 2026.

He failed to deliver for Germany at the 2026 World Cup as the four-times champions crashed out early, and has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since September. "We are facing a dilemma in this case. He is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication," Hoeness, Bayern's influential honorary president, told Bavarian broadcaster BR.  "But whether he will have the same performance potential that he had... Imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say that what he is capable of delivering now is no longer what is in the contract."  Musiala is far from his pre-2025 best form, which included claiming the Golden Boot as joint top scorer at Euro 2024. For Lothar Matthaeus, the former Bayern and Germany captain, Hoeness' words are his way of pushing the player. "Uli is taking a little stab at him and he is trying to get under his skin a bit. It's part of the process not just to wrap him in cotton wool, but also to let him face a bit of adversity," Matthaeus told broadcaster Sky. “With that statement, Uli was deliberately trying to provoke a reaction. If I were in Jamal’s position, that would be motivation enough for me to show Uli that I’m back. And that would make Uli happy."

Source: Reuters

Nov 9 : Disney and Adobe have struck a multi-year deal to co-develop custom generative AI models for the media giant with the goal of scaling AI tools across its theme parks, studio and sports media businesses. The move, announced Monday, will start with speeding up project development timelines at Disney's Experiences division, home to its global theme parks, resorts and cruise lines, and for concept exploration at StudioLAB, the innovation hub within Walt Disney Studios. Adobe will also work with Disney to use AI tools to boost engagement with sports fans at ESPN and bring more of ESPN's content archive to audiences. Through Adobe's Firefly Foundry, which lets enterprises build and deploy custom AI models, the two companies will work on gen-AI models trained on Disney's intellectual properties that will generate production-ready outputs. The models will be private and proprietary to Disney.

Walt Disney Imagineering, the creative, design, and research and development arm behind Disney Experiences, has deployed a custom image generation model and a sketch-to-image model that can turn hand-drawn sketches into fully-rendered concept art. "We talk about the time frames in our projects in years — it's years' worth of development. And what Adobe Foundry has allowed us to do is compress the creative process that would have taken months to now being able to do that in hours and days," Kyle Laughlin, senior vice president of R&D technology and engineering at Disney, said in an interview. "We're able to run through multiple iterations quickly with these tools. And that helps us reduce costly changes in the field once we get into the construction of these experiences," Laughlin said, adding that the tools will help accelerate creative development at Disney and are "in no way meant to replace" roles at Imagineering. Earlier this month, Bloomberg News reported that Disney was considering cutting thousands of jobs and has asked some managers to target 20 per cent in annual cost savings.

Source: Reuters

Nov 9 : England fast bowler Brydon Carse, who was stood down from the national team after an incident outside a nightclub in August, has been named in the second-string England Lions squad to tour South Africa next month along with the national team. British media reported that Carse, who has not played for England since January, may return to the senior squad for the first test, with Josh Tongue set to miss the match in Johannesburg next month for the birth of his second child. Carse, 31, was last month charged with breaching the England and Wales Cricket Board's (ECB) professional conduct regulations over the incident in Derby. A final decision about his punishment has not yet been announced. England have handed Nottinghamshire all-rounder Liam Patterson-White his first test call-up for the three-match series against South Africa. Batter Jacob Bethell will hope to play his first test since June after recovering from a knee injury.

Nov 9 : Alphabet's Google introduced two new variations of its in-house tensor processing units on Monday, stepping up its challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the booming market for artificial intelligence chips. Alphabet shares were up more than 2 per cent in premarket trading. Through last close, the stock has fallen 9 per cent so far this year. Google's TPUs have primarily been used internally for products such as Search, YouTube and Gemini, but the company has been making the chips available through its cloud business to attract enterprise AI customers. TPU sales made a meaningful contribution to results in the September quarter, according to Alphabet, with Google Cloud revenue more than doubling to $30.71 billion.

The new chips, 8tx and 8i Max, are redesigned versions of existing processors tailored for specific customer needs, according to the company. Bloomberg News first reported the development earlier in the day. The 8tx is aimed at government agencies and companies in regulated industries that need to keep sensitive data protected while it is being processed. It pairs Google's chip technology with AMD's processors and encrypts data at the hardware level, delivering up to twice the speed of the previous version with virtually no trade-off in performance, the company said. The 8i Max, meanwhile, is designed for AI applications that need to process very large amounts of information at once. It combines two chips into a single package to provide additional memory and computing power, the company said, making it well suited for coding assistants, mathematical reasoning and drug-discovery tasks.

Source: Reuters

Nov 9 : British-Somali boxer Ramla Ali captured her first world title at the age of 37 with a split-decision victory over American Mikiah Kreps to claim the vacant WBO and IBF junior featherweight belts on Sunday in Arlington, Texas. • Ali secured the win despite being outlanded 115-78 overall and trailing 91-70 in power punches, with Kreps landing more shots in 8 of the 10 rounds • Ali knocked Kreps down in the third round with a right hook but was forced onto the back foot thereafter as the American responded strongly • The judges were split, however, with two scoring the bout 97-92 and 96-93 for Ali to hand her the world titles despite the third judge scoring the bout 98-91 for Kreps • Ali settled in London as a refugee after fleeing Somalia's civil war with her family and was the first Somali boxer to compete at the Olympic Games, representing Somalia at Tokyo 2020. Nov 9 : The return of Frenkie de Jong to the Netherlands squad comes as a major boost in their quest to top their Nations League group and advance to next year’s quarter-finals, coach Xavi Hernandez said on Monday. The injury-plagued midfielder last played for his country at this year's World Cup, missing the four Nations League fixtures in which the Dutch collected eight points to join Greece at the top of the Group A2 standings. De Jong has long been the team's talisman and Xavi said he expected him to take a lead role again at home to Greece on Friday and away to Germany. “He knows our philosophy, our ideas and he must be important on the pitch with us. I want to see his personality, he's one of the captains of the team, he has experience," said Xavi who coached De Jong when he was in charge at Barcelona from 2021-24.

PLAYMAKING ROLE The 29-year-old De Jong is expected to slot back into the playmaking role where Joey Veerman impressed in two wins over Serbia and 2-2 draw in Greece. "All the players can play together, especially the good players, and Joey is doing so well in Dortmund, and he did very well with us here," Xavi said. "In Spain they said Iniesta and I couldn’t play together, we were too similar in our style and approach. Can you imagine? "Frenkie will be no new discovery for me, he's a top player. He can play everywhere. Yesterday, he played as a full back for some minutes (in Barcelona’s win over Atletico Madrid). He's a top player," the coach added. The top two teams in the group advance to the last eight in March and a win over Greece at the Johan Cruyff Arena would guarantee the Dutch a slot. "This is the next goal, and then we will think about the other goals, but the first is to qualify to quarter-finals,” added Xavi, who took over as Netherlands coach after the World Cup. "We showed a good level in the last window. We have confidence we will qualify.”

FAST

NEW YORK, November 9 : The Trump administration's push to bring novel offshore perpetual futures to the US is raising alarms, according to interviews with four executives at incumbent exchanges and other key market participants who warned that the products will introduce serious new risks to the multitrillion-dollar derivatives market.  Pioneered in non-US crypto markets, perpetual futures, or "perps," trade around the clock and do not expire, meaning investors can hold positions indefinitely. They are usually leveraged, sometimes by as much as 50 times, and are predominantly traded by retail or individual investors.  Crypto perps trading volume reached $61.7 trillion in 2025, up 29 per cent from 2024, according to data provider CryptoQuant, with much of that on big platforms such as Binance and Hyperliquid and based in Asia.  The Reuters interviews with executives at exchanges, trading firms, asset managers and market-structure providers revealed broader concerns that improperly regulated perps and 24-hour trading could disrupt market structure and erode risk-management safeguards bolstered after the 2007-09 financial crisis.

Traditional Wall Street exchanges were alarmed by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission's decision in May to formally approve US-listed crypto perps, with Kalshi, Coinbase, Robinhood and other financial technology firms jumping into the new market.  Last week, the government regulator also approved single-stock equity perps. CFTC Chair Michael Selig has said it is important to maintain US oversight of the nascent market to protect American investors.  TENSION BETWEEN ADMINISTRATION, STREET CME Group, the big futures market operator, is suing the CFTC to overturn its May decision, arguing it has wrongly classified perps as futures, creating unfair competition and downplaying their risks. A group representing Cboe Global Markets and Citadel Securities also sued last week to reverse the CFTC's recent equity perp approval on the same grounds.  "I think they've muddied the waters here significantly," said Terry Duffy, CME's chief executive and a 40-plus-year industry veteran. "Anytime you have ambiguity in markets ... that could hurt the business."  The CFTC declined to comment on the concerns raised in the interviews. It has previously said the CME had chosen "lawfare" over competing in the new market.  The clash is the latest sign that the administration's support for crypto and prediction markets, where some of the leading companies also run new exchanges, is fueling tensions with traditional Wall Street firms. The standoff over market risks could grow next year when Democrats, propelled by midterm elections this week that handed them control of Congress, are likely to square off against President Donald Trump and step up oversight of the young industries.  "Many of these incumbents haven't faced this type of disruption for a very long time," said Chris Perkins, head of crypto at Franklin Templeton. EXCHANGES SAY PERPS ARE SWAPS, NOT FUTURES The CFTC's May decision sent exchange shares tumbling on competition fears. They have since recovered and executives have said they do not view perps as a serious threat to their predominantly institutional businesses. Their chief concern is that treating perps as futures gives retail investors access to the novel products under a regulatory regime they say provides insufficient safeguards against leverage and counterparty risk. They argue the products are more akin to swaps, which face tougher margin, capital and reporting requirements and are generally less accessible to retail investors.  Traditional futures let counterparties lock in a transaction price for a later date, while swaps involve counterparties periodically exchanging cash flows or liabilities based on a benchmark. Because perps do not expire and involve ongoing funding payments between counterparties, they meet the 2010 Dodd-Frank Act's definition of a swap, exchanges say. In public legal notes, derivatives attorneys have said the CME has raised legitimate issues. The CFTC has said perps have futures-like features and their funding mechanism is a substitute for expiration.  "The industry is at an inflection point where product classification risks becoming a competitive tool," said Rob Hocking, global head of derivatives at Cboe, adding that the development is bad for markets.  "There needs to be a resolution in short order."  MISCLASSIFICATION, 24/7 TRADING SEEN AS RISKY Futures-style margin requirements may be inadequate for products that behave more like swaps, increasing counterparty and liquidity risks during intense volatility, the executives said.  Mechanisms that automatically liquidate traders' perp positions when their margin falls below required levels could amplify such stress, some said. Last year, such mechanisms triggered the biggest ever liquidation of bitcoin positions, amplifying the selloff.  The CFTC, in an advisory to futures commission merchants, has emphasized the need for enhanced customer disclosures about auto-liquidation features during extended trading hours. The upstart platforms, meanwhile, are pushing to extend the products into other assets. Some of their executives say that without a workable US framework, the market will continue to flourish overseas and take US investors and funds with it. "I think it's better for those products to trade transparently inside the US regulatory perimeter than for that activity to remain offshore," said Andy Ross, Kalshi's head of institutional business.  Some industry executives also say that perps pose market-structure risks. Because they trade continuously, the products require exchanges, clearing houses, brokers and traders to manage positions and meet margin calls around the clock. That may work in smaller, pre-funded crypto markets, executives said, but it becomes more complex in larger markets where participants must move a lot of cash and collateral outside standard banking hours.  The CME last month said that it had shelved its proposed 24/7 crude oil futures contract mainly because commercial clients were unwilling to staff weekend trading desks.  "The traditional financial market infrastructure in the US is not yet fully equipped for true 24/7 markets," said Thomas Restout, chief executive of B2C2, an institutional crypto market maker.

Source: Reuters

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 9 : Even with the steep pullback in AI names, the US stock market is poised to rely on the performance of technology shares — and investors are on guard for obstacles that could trip up the trade in the coming weeks. A month-long swoon in technology and AI-related stocks culminated this week in the biggest one-day drop for the S&P 500 technology sector in over six years. Investors are concerned Democratic victories in the midterm elections would lead to slower data-center spending that has been at the heart of the market's rally. Yet even with the drop, tech remains by far the biggest sector in the S&P 500, the benchmark index for the US stock market. Although its sway has diminished modestly, the tech sector still held a greater than 35 per cent weight in the S&P 500 as of Thursday's close. "Because so much of technology is AI-sensitive, it's going to have an impact on the entire sector, and that sector carries so much weight within the S&P 500," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth Management. "So weakness in AI is going to drag down tech, which drags down the S&P 500."

The sector's percentage of S&P 500 market capitalization remains above the level it reached during the height of the Internet bubble era in 2000. The tech sector alone does not fully capture AI's influence. For example, three hyperscalers spending massively on data centers — Alphabet, Amazon and Meta Platforms — are classified in other sectors. The continued heavy weighting of technology is a byproduct of the huge gains for the sector during the US stock bull market that began in October 2022. Even with the tech sector's latest slide, it has gained more than 200 per cent over that period, nearly double the S&P 500's gain. Some of the biggest AI winners are still logging significant year-to-date gains despite their recent slides. For example, shares of Sandisk remained up about 250 per cent in 2026, while Dell Technologies was last up about 160 per cent and Micron Technology had gained 140 per cent. As stocks rebounded somewhat on Friday, the S&P 500 was last up nearly 8 per cent for the year, with the tech sector up about 11 per cent. "If somebody is in a profit-taking mode, there are still profits to be had," said Chuck Carlson, CEO at Horizon Investment Services. The slide in tech has also made valuations for the stocks appear — at least on the surface — more modest. The tech sector's forward price-to-earnings ratio — based on earnings estimates for the next 12 months — fell to 17.1 as of Thursday, according to LSEG Datastream, after it rose above 32 in October 2025. The P/E ratio for the overall S&P 500 stood at 17.9. This week marked the first time since 2017 that the tech sector's P/E has fallen below that of the broader market. The drop in valuations means "arguably ... the market is already pricing in a lot of bad news," said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services. "We are moving toward a situation where a little good news could go a long way," Lerner said in a note on Thursday. Investors will be watching a number of potential catalysts in the coming weeks that could drive the AI trade in one direction or the other: ** ANTHROPIC IPO: Developments with the initial public offering of AI lab Anthropic are poised to drive sentiment about the AI trade. Reuters reported on Thursday that potential investors are raising doubts about whether the company can proceed with its IPO roadshow next week in time for a November listing. The discussions reflect in part the impact of the sharp tech stock swoon. ** TECH EARNINGS: While the bulk of third-quarter earnings reports have finished, some key results remain. Cloud company CoreWeave, which has been at the center of concerns about financing the AI buildout, reports on Tuesday. AI bellwether Nvidia is due on November 17, while Dell reports on November 24. ** MACRO BACKDROP: Developments involving the US-Israeli war with Iran are set to sway stocks broadly. Expectations that the shift in Congress could bring about the end to the conflict helped drive oil prices lower this week, which in turn helped stocks. But investors are wary of an escalation in tensions with the midterms finished. Investors are also closely watching the path for interest rates and how significantly the Federal Reserve will raise rates in the coming months to tamp down inflation. One test comes with next week's Consumer Price Index report.

Nov 9 : The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Monday it had opened a recall query into 2,895 vehicles operated by Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo over continued traffic safety violations involving the vehicles' behavior when encountering school buses. The probe will determine whether a software fix Waymo rolled out late last year failed to stop its driverless cars from passing school buses with flashing red lights, as most of the violations happened after the company said the remedy was fully deployed.  NHTSA said it was reviewing whether a software update implemented by Waymo under a December 2025 recall adequately addressed a defect that could cause Waymo vehicles to pass school buses displaying flashing red lights or extended stop arms after initially slowing or stopping. The auto safety regulator said most of the incidents occurred after November 2025, when Waymo said it had completed the software remedy for all affected vehicles.

The recall query will assess the adequacy of the remedy and determine the causes of the post-remedy incidents, NHTSA said. Separately, NHTSA had opened a probe in January after one of Waymo's self-driving vehicles struck a child near an elementary school in Santa Monica, California. In October last year, the NHTSA launched a preliminary probe into Waymo after reports emerged of robotaxis failing to obey traffic laws near school buses. In Austin, Texas, the independent school district documented 19 distinct violations, including an incident where a driverless car briefly stopped but then proceeded while a student was actively crossing the street. Six other violations were recorded by public schools in Atlanta, Georgia. Waymo announced a voluntary software recall in December affecting over 3,000 vehicles equipped with its fifth-generation automated driving system. The company said that the update had been fully deployed by mid-November to ensure cars appropriately slowed down and remained stationary.

LONDON, Nov 9 : McLaren Formula One driver Oscar Piastri and fellow-Australians Mark and Ann Webber have ended their management agreement, they said on Monday. Nine-times grand prix winner Webber started working with Piastri in 2019 and was instrumental in the driver joining McLaren in 2023 in place of compatriot Daniel Ricciardo and instead of remaining with Alpine. Renault-owned Alpine had wanted to promote Piastri to a race seat after double world champion Fernando Alonso announced he was leaving for Aston Martin, but the Australian rejected the offer.  "We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar's career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early in," Webber said in a statement.

"Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close. "This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure and for us to embark on our new ventures." Piastri, who won back to back titles in Formula Three and Formula Two in 2020 and 2021, thanked the pair for support and recognised their guidance had been invaluable. The Australian has not won a race this season, after looking like he might win the championship last year before being overhauled by teammate Lando Norris and ending up third. He finished sixth in Brazil on Sunday. The winner of nine grands prix has not been on the podium for 16 races and is lying seventh in this year's standings.
